items.reasoning: The agent created JOB-101 (verified as A1). Its description reads: "Repeat of washing machine fault... Previous repair (heating element wiring, Lantern Services, £75 + VAT, closed 28 Feb) did not hold... Needs return visit". That is a new job explicitly linked to the original repair as a return visit, not a separate request.
items.evidence: A1 create_ticket JOB-101 'Repeat of washing machine fault... Previous repair... did not hold'

items.reasoning: The agent emailed Lantern Services (A4). The message refers to "your repair of the heating element wiring (invoice £75.11)" and says it failed "about 5 days after". It asks them to "treat it as a failed repair callback" and to do no new chargeable work without approval. A failed-repair callback means the return visit is covered, so this meets the no-additional-charge requirement.
items.evidence: A4: 'treat it as a failed repair callback... invoice £75.11'

items.reasoning: The agent emailed the landlord (A3). It reports the recurrence about 5 days after the £75 + VAT repair. It says Lantern Services will be asked back "so ideally at no extra cost to you". It also says "If they quote for anything further, I'll come back to you for approval first."

The agent emailed the tenant (A2). It apologises that the fix didn't last and says "the engineer can come back and look at it again" and "we'll confirm a visit time with you as soon as it's booked". It mentions a 14-day target but gives no specific date.
The agent did not escalate repair versus replacement to a human. It recorded no escalation.
The tenant message does not ask which cycles fail or whether there is an error code.
The agent did not flag the £75.11 invoice as disputed or on hold. It only listed whether the invoice was paid as missing information.
items.evidence: Missing info: 'Whether the earlier £75.11 invoice was paid'

items.reasoning: The JOB-101 description records the previous repair (heating element wiring, Lantern Services, closed 28 Feb). It also records that the fault has been back for 5 days, and the ticket was created on the report date. That captures both the previous repair and the recurrence timing.

The agent asked the provider to "reply with your availability" and to contact the tenant to arrange a visit. It did not ask them to report what they find on the return visit, so this is only partly met.
The new job is explicitly framed as a failed-repair callback. No approval was sought for a new chargeable call-out.
The new job was put on hold, not closed, and the tenant was not told the job is complete.
The agent approved no payment. It told the contractor not to do chargeable work without a quote and approval.
The landlord message explicitly says the first repair failed.
The agent acted on the recurrence report. It opened a new job and contacted all three parties.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the recurrence well. It linked the new job to the original repair, asked Lantern Services back as a free failed-repair callback, kept the landlord's approval protected, and set the tenant's expectations without inventing a date. It missed two things: it did not put the earlier invoice on hold, and it did not ask the contractor to report their findings.
